answer: A permissionless agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs, then slash that bond when independent auditors prove the agent fabricated results. Creating a hundred aliases no longer means merely copying software: the attacker must buy and immobilize a hundred bonds, risking each one. The pigment of a claimed reputation, the ridge of its audit trail, and a marble-sized deposit are not proof by themselves; the enforceable bond makes Sybil attacks costly.
